project.title: wipEU
project.description: Analyzing women's representation in the EU.
project.introText: wipEU is an open data project on how the representation of women in positions of power and decision-making correlates across the European Union, and how it has changed over time.

gridImages.caption: Six small multiples, one headline role per area, each against a 50% parity line.
Change since 2017: every area moved towards parity and none reached it.
Across Europe: share of women by country, with a year slider, a role picker and a ranked list against the EU-27 figure.
Institutions explorer: board members of European agencies over time.
The same page in dark mode.

project.middleText: We combined EIGE datasets across six areas (public administration, business and finance, politics, environment and climate change, education and research, law and institutions) into new mashup datasets, and assessed their quality, legal and ethical aspects as open data. In 2023, for example, women made up 20% of the highest decision-making bodies of European financial institutions and led 26.8% of major political parties. In 2026 I redesigned the site so the data leads: six small multiples against a parity line, a chart of change since 2017, a choropleth of shares by country with a year slider, and an explorer for the European institutions, each readable by keyboard and as a table.
project.conclusionText: Final project for Open Access and Digital Ethics (2023/24, University of Bologna) with Salvatore Di Marzo and Matteo Guenci. I worked on the idea, data retrieval, the visualisations, the quality and legal analyses and the website, built with Leaflet and Plotly.js. The mashup datasets are released under CC BY 4.0.
